messages:
anna: Heads up — noticed a p99 spike on prod continuous-batcher when requests include tool calls + structured outputs. Anyone else seeing this?

mike: Yup, I noticed it around 11:12UTC. p95 looks fine but p99 doubled for decode latency. linked a couple traces I saw.

anna: trace: https://redwood/traces/abc123 — profiler shows frequent kernel swaps mid-batch and a higher KV miss rate whenever tool pauses happen. Snippet from profiler:

```
batch_id=wx-9    mean_batch=12    p99_batch=64
kernel_swap_count=2.1 per_batch
kv_miss_ratio=0.28
fragmentation_count=17
```

jin: This smells like stop-token / toolcall fragmentation. When a function-call pause happens we yield the decode, which creates many tiny fragments that hit short-seq kernel selection. Short kernels + frequent swaps = tail blowup.

olga: Also seeing KV cache churn. When fragments are small we don't get good prefix reuse and pinning TTL gets invalidated. Sampling counters from the node that flapped:

KV_EVICT=37, KV_MISS=142, pinned_hits=19, fragments_per_min=13

sam: Quick repro command to force the pause pattern (dev only):

curl -X POST https://staging.redwood/api/generate -d '{"input":"...","call_tool":true,"structured":true}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $DEV'

mike: @anna can you try lowering continuous_batcher.target_token_budget from 64 -> 40 and enable hold_prefetch=true? In a small staging run this reduced kernel swaps. Config snippet:

```yaml
continuous_batcher:
  target_token_budget: 40
  hold_prefetch: true
```

anna: Ran a 2h local run with target_token_budget=40. p99 dropped ~25% but p95 degraded slightly. Batch shape skewed to more small batches; profiler output: 

batch_shape: [1: 48%, 2-8: 36%, >8:16%]
kernel_swap_avg: 0.9 -> 0.6

jin: Another option: route requests with structured:true/toolcall to a separate queue with looser batching but pinned KV cache. Costlier but reduces tail. We can canary that for 10% traffic.

perf-bot: perf-alert: regression detected on commit sha=abcdef123. delta +18% p99 for continuous-batcher on toolcall workload. Ticket: #4567

olga: GPU timeline shows kernel thrash — kernel swaps per batch 0.7 -> 2.4 when pauses present. If we delay kernel selection until fragment end or provide a same-kernel fallback for short fragments we might avoid the thrash.

sam: Plan proposal: run A/B canary:
A) target_token_budget=48 + hold_prefetch=true + pin_kv_for_structured=true
B) separate queue for structured/toolcall (10% canary) with pinned KV and looser batching
Owners: @anna run experiments, @jin open kernel-fallback PR, @olga monitor KV metrics. Run window 8h.

anna: Ack — starting canary on staging now (config A). Will post results in ~6h. Thanks :thumbsup:
